background_story: Hezekiah, a wise and just king of ancient Judah, implemented a series of reforms that would have a lasting impact on his kingdom. One of his most notable decisions was to retroactively abolish the debts of his people, freeing them from the burden of usury. This bold move was a response to the widespread poverty and inequality that had plagued the land for generations. By wiping the slate clean, Hezekiah gave his people a second chance, allowing them to start anew and rebuild their lives. His retroactive decree was seen as a divine intervention, and it earned him the admiration and gratitude of his subjects. Hezekiah's legacy as a champion of the poor and oppressed endured for centuries, inspiring future leaders to follow in his footsteps.
